_doc: THE subagent model-choice rules, and the facts they rest on. hooks/claude/agent_guard.py enforces `tiers`, `exempt_agent_types` and `exploration`; scripts/agent_audit.py prices the ledger with `facts.price.*` and judges with `verdict`; scripts/model_choice_watch.py re-checks every fact's `check` against its source each week and marks the facts that no longer match (and the tiers resting on them) `re-research` in its findings. Nothing else restates these values (tests/test_model_choice_rules.py). Every value here is the OWNER's: the audit and the watch PROPOSE changes with their numbers, and nothing writes this file but a person (owner ruling 2026-10-18). The decision and its evidence: ~/.claude/skills/agent-fanout/references/model-choice-decision.md.

profiles._doc: Which of the rules above are in force: the plan the owner pays for, narrowed by the budget guard. `declared` is the owner's plan, set by a person and by nothing else; `order` runs from the plan with the most headroom to the least, and the guard drops ONE step along it when the meter says the headroom is not there. Each profile's `changes` are laid over the top-level `tiers`, `pool_first` and `exploration` (a dict merges key by key, anything else replaces), so `max` -- no changes -- is the rules above exactly. model_choice.py resolves the active profile; agent_guard.py names it, and why it is active, in every refusal; scripts/model_choice_watch.py's usage review proposes moving `declared` or a profile's values with the week's numbers, and never edits this file.
profiles.decided: owner 2026-11-15 (queue GOH.ULTRARULES): the Claude Ultra plan replaced Max -- 'All four' (the four ultra changes below), then the same day: "keep pro/max / ultra profiles. reevaluate the rules on a regular cadence to fit the actual usage". Approved this once as written here; later changes are proposals the owner applies.

measured.reading: a week on max rules spent ~96% of an API-equivalent $5,669 on Opus and left 95% of the 7-day meter: price, the reason behind the cheap tiers and the pool line on write spawns, was not the constraint; 600 of 615 spawns wrote `Pool: unfit` (the line was ceremony on write work); the machine, at load 118-139 on 16 cores, was

budget_guard.why: token-pool's meter (pool/meter.py; the 7-day window is the plan's binding one) below 30% left, a reading older than 6 h, or one that cannot be read drops the declared profile ONE step along `order`: a plan whose headroom cannot be seen is not spent as if it were there

review.why: the weekly usage review (scripts/model_choice_watch.py): a week whose LOWEST 7d reading stayed at or over `up_min_left_pct` proposes the next profile up (with `pool_unfit_share` of spawns writing `Pool: unfit` as its evidence that the pool line is ceremony on write work); a week whose lowest reading fell under the guard's `min_left_pct` proposes the next profile down; a 1-minute load over `load_per_core` x cores when an agent landed proposes fewer gate slots (GOH_GATE_SLOTS, machine config: lib/gate_slot.py)

max.about: today's rules exactly (the plan before 2026-11-15): every tier weighs the pool, the cheap tiers alternate

ultra.about: max plus four changes, measured on the week above: (1) pool-first narrows to read-only work; (2) the cheap first try is opus@medium; (3) at most 2 heavy gates at once machine-wide (machine config, lib/gate_slot.py, not a profile value); (4) the budget guard

sonnet@high.why: ultra: opus@medium solves more (86.6% of repo tasks vs sonnet@high 77.8%); price was its only reason, and the meter, not price, is the plan's limit

opus@low.why: ultra: opus@medium solves more (86.6% vs opus@low 74.8%); price was its only reason, and one escalation to opus@high stays (low-then-high 97% vs all-high 95.3%)

pro.about: stricter than max, for a plan whose meter is the limit: a pool line on every tier (as max), sonnet@high the default write tier (77.8% at $0.33 per attempt: it solves more than opus@low for less), opus only for the hard tags (root cause, design, audit, research, security: the pool's `hard` class)

opus@low.why: pro: sonnet@high solves more for less (77.8% at $0.33 vs opus@low 74.8% at $0.35 per attempt)

exempt_agent_types.why: read-only lookups and meta agents, and `fork`, which ignores `model`: none lands commits, so they need no model and get no contract; their spawns are still ledgered

pool_first.decided: owner 2026-10-25: read-only bulk work and checkable edits go through token-pool's `ask` (~/Projects/token-pool: free Zen, agy and Gemini quota) BEFORE a Claude subagent is spawned for them. A spawn on these tiers says which in its prompt: `Pool: tried <what ask returned>` (escalate_to_caller, a failed proof) or `Pool: unfit because <reason>` (the work needs this repo's tools: it edits, builds or runs tests, which pool's backends never do: they get the prompt and the `files` the pool inlines, nothing else). The ledger keeps the line, so a habit of `unfit` shows up as data. Owner 2026-11-01, widening it to EVERY tier a spawn may take, opus included: "Next time don't wait for me to prompt you to use agy". A review, an audit or a root-cause read that agy could answer from the files went to Opus because opus tiers needed no line; now every spawn weighs the pool (the opus tiers' class is `hard`, or `second_opinion` for a read-only review).

cheap_alternation.decided: owner 2026-10-18 (goh model-choice improvement loop, item 3): a checkable + known-fix spawn runs on whichever cheap tier the parity of its prompt's sha picks, so the two are compared on the same kind of work

opus_to_cheap.decided: OWNER DECISION PENDING (2026-10-18): default OFF. When on, this fraction of opus@medium spawns that declare `checkable` (and not `unchecked`) run on the cheap tier instead; escalation bounds the cost. A spawn without a mechanical check is never routed down, on or off.

lean_types.measured: 2026-11-08 (GOH.LEANAGENT): median first-turn context of a general-purpose agent 70.6k tokens, of which ~65k is fixed preamble (every MCP server's tool names, the deferred-tool and agent-type lists); repo-worker lists its tools, so only CLAUDE.md, the skills list and its own tools load
lean_types.decided: owner 2026-11-08 (queue GOH.LEANAGENT): a write spawn of a `from` type is refused with the lean type to use (`to`, or `ui` for on-screen QA); a read-only lookup (`read_only_tiers`) is not steered. Escape: `Agent-type: <the type> because <reason>` in the prompt, kept on the ledger as `agent_type_escape`. The types are installed by scripts/apply_claude_hooks.py from hooks/claude/agents/.

verdict.rule: a cheap class holds while its redo rate < 1 - (its cost per attempt / the escalation class's cost per attempt); cost = the ledger's tokens x facts.price.<model>
